deposits.genre_observed: theoretical paper on Plato–Aristotle authorship (reading copy) with attached pass registers and measurement apparatus

finds.quote:
**ONE PERSON WROTE THIS.** That is the claim of this paper, and nothing
above dissolves, replaces, or spiritualises it.

**⚠ And "person" is not here defined as "one body."** The paper does not require the maker to be individuated biologically, and §§I–V have spent five sections showing that what counts as one depends on the mode of unity. **What is claimed is that however the maker is divided — by voice, by object, by name, by position — the divisions are of ONE PERSON and not an aggregation of several.**
finds.falsifier_quote: Only one of them can be checked against the text by the corpus-internal methods used here; the other asks how many embodied makers there were, and that question lives in the external record — papyrology [VIII.4], inscriptions, transmission history — which this paper does not touch.**
finds.window: in Athens, in the fourth century
finds.note: The paper's central historical thesis: one person wrote the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora; stated as claimed but not recoverable from text; external record named as where it would be decided.

finds.quote: **The reading this argument takes, and it is the configurational one.** **οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν** is literal because there was no predecessor: **the divisional apparatus is the same maker's earlier work, developed before he knew what it could divide.**
finds.note: Thesis about what SE 34's priority claim originally meant: literal, because the divisional apparatus in the Platonic corpus is the same maker's earlier work.

finds.quote:
> **Four words, four readings, every one paid for on Aristotle's side of the
> ledger. The fourth word has never been moved for Plato.**
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: every traditional reading of APr I.31/SE 34 moves a word on Aristotle's side; the received filling has never been examined as a choice.

finds.quote:
> **THE DEPARTURE IS ONE SENTENCE. Where Kahn reads the corpus as one author (Plato)
> deploying a literary character (Socrates), the configurational reading identifies
> Socrates as an authorial POSITION in his own right** — not a character within a
> project but the position the project is organised around.
finds.note: Adopts and extends Kahn: Socrates as an authorial position the corpus is organised around, not a character.

finds.quote:
> **The claim here is not that the problem is solved. It is that under a functional
> lens it appears as a SYMPTOM rather than a problem** — the predictable trace of a
> configuration the biographical model cannot represent.
finds.note: Thesis about the Socratic problem: a symptom of a configuration rather than a problem; argued, with the firewall's limits.

finds.quote:
Nothing of the
questioning method, the ignorance-as-position, or the midwifery is in the comic
layer. **Comedy supplied the notoriety — a name with a reputation attached, in public
circulation a generation before the trial — and the later corpus occupied the
position and differentiated it:** defendant, questioner, midwife, reported master,
absent centre.
finds.note: Thesis on Aristophanes' Clouds and the Platonic Socrates: comedy supplied the notoriety, the later corpus occupied and differentiated the position; marked as a reading beyond the uncontroversial account.

finds.quote: *So the defensible statement is narrow: attendance, on the earliest evidence — which is also the earliest evidence of the break (the Lyceum in opposition while Plato lived, Vita Marciana §25) — with the devoted-pupil picture a later construction resting on a lost letter and a Life that cannot keep its own chronology.
finds.window: Vita Marciana §5, §25; Aristotle born 384, Socrates died 399
finds.note: Thesis on the Plato–Aristotle teaching relation: not internally attested; the devoted-pupil picture is a later construction.

finds.quote: **This paper explains it by a program:** a sequence of forms, walked in the order the corpus sets out at *Symposium* 210 — one body, all bodies, souls, practices and laws, the knowledges, and the thing itself. **With each rung a recognition of unity at a wider scope, and none of them an accumulation of parts.**
finds.falsifier_quote:
> **THE NEXT TEST, STATED SO IT CAN BE RUN AGAINST THIS PAPER:** define the proposed
> form-track **independently of the stylometric variables** — from explicit generic,
> argumentative or object-level criteria — and test whether the corpus orders along
> it. **If it does, the old chronology effect was tracking repertoire. Until then,
> the repertoire reading gives the contaminated result a new meaning and does not
> remove the contamination.**
finds.note: Thesis that the corpus's order is of genre and form (and of grasp), not chronology/biography; the form-track test is its falsifier (also recorded as F).

finds.quote: **So the received account already requires one man in two registers** — the Platonic dialogue register and the treatise register — **and has lost the register-crossing half entirely**, while Plato's dialogue corpus survives complete, spuria included.
finds.note: Thesis from Cicero's testimony: the received account concedes a one-man two-register capacity and has lost the register-crossing half; null on transmission stated at ¶27.

finds.quote: **The corpus with complete coverage of the predecessors is the channel through which the predecessors survive.** It lived, in part, by being what later readers needed in order to reach what came before it.
finds.note: Transmission thesis: the Presocratics survive through the Aristotelian corpus, so the standard for checking the corpus reaches us through it; null (first historian of philosophy) stated.

finds.quote: **The reading at Round 44 — that Longinus *extends* rather than cuts, and Catullus discharges the grammatical obligation the extension creates — is this paper's and requires the extension to be deliberate.**
finds.note: Thesis on transmission of Sappho 31: Longinus extends the quotation one clause, and Catullus 51's otium stanza discharges the obligation it creates; offered as new, against the standard account.

finds.quote: What wants explaining is that this corpus survived **with its disputes, its spuria, its unresolved attributions and its unnamed genre intact** — with all the machinery that makes it require continued work. **Most surviving corpora shed that machinery. This one kept it** — *which is the comparative claim the survival table (§6) would test and has not; until it is run, this is a description of one corpus.*
finds.note: Comparative historical thesis that this corpus survived with its disputes and spuria intact where most shed that machinery; marked untested (survival table / Reynolds–Wilson comparison).

finds.quote: *So the single remaining line of Socrates-attestation outside the cluster sits in a forgery whose author was demonstrably reading Plato.*
finds.note: Thesis that Socrates' attestation outside the four-corpus cluster reduces to a lost pamphlet and a Plato-reading forgery.

finds.quote: **And the vacant centre becomes a specification rather than a loss:** in an accidental fragmentation the whole is simply gone; in a ratified one the centre is **implied by the fit** and need never be occupied by a writing position at all. *On this logic, Socrates not writing stops being an absence in the evidence and becomes the form the centre necessarily takes.*
finds.note: Reconstruction (marked as such, under the firewall) of Socrates' not writing as the form of the corpus's centre.

finds.quote: > **What made him look like many authors is that he wrote about many things.**
finds.note: Thesis on Aristotle's internal dispersion: object-conditioned, not many-authored; measured (0.0571 vs 0.0570), with the school caveat at ¶19.

finds.quote:
**Stated in advance:** if Plato→Aristotle had fallen **below the heteronymic floor** — outside the constructed-configuration range on the size-matched features — the configurational reading would have been damaged in the ordinary way, and the paper would say so here.

**20.** **It did not happen.** The target sits inside the range. **That is not confirmation and it is not nothing: it is a test that could have gone the other way and went this way.**
finds.points_to: stated in advance (R52 §232(c), per the notebook reread register)
finds.note: Records a falsifier set in advance and reports that it did not fire.

finds.quote: **The falsification programme is stated and open:** eight directly-attested contact pairs, each scorable on the same three properties; **one pair producing unannounced, sequence-kept, transformative interlock across an apparatus kills the claim.** Williams→Ginsberg is the sharpest unrun — the master wrote the introduction to *Howl*, announcement by the master being what direct contact characteristically produces.
finds.note: Standing claim (schools default to announced commentary, not unannounced interlock) with explicit kill condition; Williams→Ginsberg named as the sharpest unrun pair.

finds.quote: **Named in-text and unrun, so they can be run against this paper:** the residual-vs-total parity base rate; the remainder test on the target; the Williams→Ginsberg pair; the four-functional-roles measurement; the FLAT-ambiguity discriminator; the validation suite itself.
finds.note: List of unrun tests named in the paper (residual-vs-total base rate, remainder test, Williams→Ginsberg, four functional roles, FLAT discriminator, validation suite); one F per rule 4.

finds.note: Independent form-track test of the corpus's ordering, specified and not run.

finds.quote:
> **What distinguishes what survived from what was lost, from the same period and the
> same tradition — and does this corpus carry those properties at a rate others do
> not?**
finds.note: Survival table from Diogenes Laertius' book-lists, with four feasibility conditions; explicitly not run.

finds.quote: **It has not been consulted by this investigation and is named as the standing external check** — the kind of evidence §VIII says would bear on the question and this paper does not have.
finds.note: Papyrological record (CPF) named as the standing external check, not consulted.

finds.quote: **Both corpora close on what individuates Socrates.** ⚠ *A coincidence until a base rate is run, and none has been; recorded, not argued from.*
finds.note: Closing-symmetry observation awaiting a base rate that has not been run.

finds.quote: *The falsifiable form is the shape of the ambiguity: natural non-resolution is uneven — evidence accumulates directionally, instruments move the needle — while engineered unresolvability would be FLAT, stalling at the same place regardless of instrument and not closing under rising attention. That discriminator is stated and has not been run.*
finds.note: FLAT-ambiguity discriminator (engineered vs natural non-resolution); also listed in the 3452 list but quoted here at its fullest statement.
